title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: AI-visibility category mints its first unicorn — Profound closes a $96M Series C at ~$1B valuation, tracking 10+ AI engines on 400M+ prompt insights
bullets.summary: Profound sits at the enterprise end of a GEO/AEO field of 8+ platforms with a 92/100 AEO score, SOC 2 Type II, Prompt Volumes panel data on what users actually ask AI systems, and Agent Analytics on how AI crawlers read a site. The raise confirms AI-visibility is a funded, consolidating software category now.
bullets.how: The moat clock for PRAGMA. The measurement layer (does an engine name you) is being commoditized by a well-funded incumbent; PRAGMA's defensible ground is the doing — answer-shaping content + schema + attribution — not another dashboard. Sequence the land-grab before the category's defaults harden around Profound.

bullets.title: GEO/AEO becomes a measurable discipline — Gartner's 25% search-decline-by-2026 prediction is now reality; enterprises track AI-answer visibility as a KPI
bullets.summary: The framing landing with buyers: GEO is 80% strategic (positioning, ecosystem presence, brand authority) and only 20% technical — structuring content so ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Claude cite and recommend you.
bullets.how: Validates the PRAGMA 'Sauce' loop pitch almost word-for-word: the win is being named in the answer, an authority/positioning problem we already run for B9 clients. Use the '80% strategic' line in buyer copy to escape a tooling comparison against Profound.

bullets.title: Agentic CRM ships three products in one week — Affinity Ascend, SeoSamba ActionEko, TrueDialog TrueConnect/TrueOptOut — as Salesforce Agentforce hits $540M ARR / 18,500 customers
bullets.summary: The CRM layer is rapidly becoming agent-native; Agentforce is the clearest proof a pure-play agentic platform can scale commercially.
bullets.how: The buy-vs-build framework is exactly the wedge The Construct wins on: SMB clients can't afford Agentforce economics, so a single Construct pipeline/media operator agent on a CRM MCP is the affordable 'build' they buy from us.

bullets.title: Marketing automation enters the 'agent era' — 34% of enterprise marketing teams now run autonomous agents in production, double Q4 2025, copilots replacing static workflows across HubSpot/Salesforce/Klaviyo/Make
bullets.summary: Agents that plan, execute, and optimize campaigns autonomously are the default expectation; enterprise agentic AI returns ~171% ROI on average (192% US).
bullets.how: The productized-operator thesis is now market consensus, shortening the education cycle for B9/PRAGMA. Lead with ROI numbers buyers already believe; skip proving agents work at all.

bullets.title: Frontier field stays seated — no drop cleared the 24h bar; Opus 5 (Jul 24) newest above GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.5, Muse Spark 1.1
bullets.summary: MCP story still dominates (final spec RC 2026-07-28: stateless core + MCP Apps + Tasks extensions); model tier quiet. Cost/quality split unchanged: Opus 5 for reasoning-heavy jobs, Gemini 3.6 Flash for cheap high-volume batch.
bullets.how: Watch, don't switch; nothing changes the fleet's model routing this cycle.

praxis_lesson: Today the outside world put a number on PRAGMA's window. A $1B AEO-measurement unicorn (Profound) plus GEO becoming a tracked enterprise KPI means the measurement half of AI-visibility is now funded, standardized, and racing toward commodity — competing on 'we can tell you if AI names you' is a losing lane. The defensible half is the one incumbents structurally under-serve: actually making a business get named — answer-shaping content, schema, and inquiry-attribution per client, per trade, per metro — for SMBs whose economics lock them out of Profound/Agentforce pricing. Sequence the trade x metro land-grab now, lead buyer copy with '80% strategic, 20% technical' to escape the tooling comparison, and wire a single Construct operator agent to CRM/media MCPs so buy-vs-build resolves in our favor before the category's defaults harden.
